description:
The iPhone camera is cherished worldwide because it captures life’s most meaningful
moments with unmatched fidelity and artistry. Our team is dedicated to pushing those
boundaries even further.

The Image Quality Qualification team is seeking an exceptional engineer who combines deep
technical acumen in imaging science with an artistic eye for photography and cinematography.
Hands-on capture and testing are central to this role: you will spend meaningful time in the
field, shooting with pre-release devices much as customers do, and applying your technical
expertise to explore and assess specific image quality artifacts. In this role, you will help shape
the future of visual capture across Apple products—driving continuous innovation in photo and
video quality and delivering extraordinary visual experiences to hundreds of millions of users
around the globe.

Description
As an Image Quality Engineer, you will sit at the intersection of art and engineering, working
cross-functionally to evaluate, refine, and champion next-generation camera features and
computational photography pipelines. You will design and execute rigorous experimental
studies—both within state-of-the-art laboratory environments and in the field, across a variety
of real-world scenes, lighting conditions, and environments—to validate cutting-edge
algorithms and imaging architectures.

A notable part of your work will involve taking devices into the field to recreate authentic user
captures, thoughtfully targeting specific image quality artifacts, and sharing your assessments
with the team. You can look forward to regular hands-on capture and testing, with occasional
travel.

Your insights and critical eye will directly influence technologies such as Portrait mode,
advanced video workflows, and emerging capture methodologies. Working within a high-
energy, collaborative, and fast-paced team, you will turn complex subjective perceptions into
actionable engineering feedback, ensuring every feature meets Apple’s exacting standards for
image excellence.

Responsibilities
Experimental Design & Evaluation: Design, execute, and oversee comprehensive objective and perceptual image and video quality evaluations across diverse shooting environments and lighting conditions, including meaningful hands-on field capture.

User Experience Advocacy: Develop a rich understanding of how people use iPhone cameras in everyday life, and draw on it to recreate real-world use cases and surface corner cases. Bring together image quality and user experience perspectives, testing in the field as a user would.

Algorithm & Pipeline Validation: Partner closely with algorithm, ISP, and software engineering teams to evaluate new computational photography features, oﬀering precise, data-driven feedback and visual defect diagnosis.

Core 3A & Tuning Assessment: Systematically stress-test and benchmark core camera behaviors, including Auto Exposure (AE), Auto Focus (AF), and Auto White Balance (AWB) across realistic and edge-case scenarios.

Laboratory & Instrumentation Leadership: Calibrate and operate sophisticated optical and photographic lab equipment to maintain rigorous, repeatable measurement standards.

Cross-Functional Advocacy: Articulate nuanced visual quality findings through clear technical reports, data visualizations, and executive demonstrations to drive consensus across engineering disciplines.

Minimum qualifications
Experience with hands-on field capture and testing of photo and video features, and enthusiasm for spending time shooting on location.

Deep practical knowledge of camera systems and core 3A behaviors (Auto Exposure, Auto Focus, Auto White Balance) in laboratory and real-world environments.

Refined visual sensibility and deep technical fluency in photography, videography, and cinematography, paired with an instinctive understanding of the elements of exceptional visual storytelling.

Solid grounding in the Human Visual System (HVS) and the perceptual psychophysics governing how real-world scenes translate into perceived image fidelity.

Hands-on proficiency operating and calibrating benchtop optical instrumentation, studio lighting, standard test charts, and specialized imaging lab equipment.

B.S. or M.S. in Imaging Science, Color Science, Vision Science, Optical Engineering, Computer Science, or equivalent practical experience, with 3+ years of industry experience in imaging or camera systems.

Preferred qualifications
Proven proficiency in Python or MATLAB for scientific computing, image processing pipelines, data visualization, and test automation.

Direct experience conducting both subjective psychophysical user studies and objective image quality metrics (e.g., MTF/SFR, color accuracy/ΔE, SNR/noise profiling, dynamic range, and tone reproduction).

Comprehensive understanding of end-to-end camera architectures, spanning sensor physics, lens optics, Image Signal Processors (ISP), and modern computational photography frameworks.

Superb written, visual, and verbal communication skills, with a demonstrated ability to foster collaboration across multidisciplinary hardware, software, and creative teams.
